Opening the VLP Maths Tools…

VLP Maths Tools PRIMARYVersion 20.1 · 24 November 2026

Settings

Saved in this browser. A school can set these once and share them with Save a copy for your school (under Branding).

Year overviewSave, load, print or check your changes

Save or load

All three tabs share one year overview. Save it to a file to keep a copy, move it to another computer, or give your team the same program. Loading a file changes the year overview in all three tabs for the levels in the file.

Print on A3

One A3 landscape page. Choose Save as PDF in the print window for a PDF.

Your changes

BrandingYour school's name, logo and colours

Your school's name, logo and colours on these tools, and in the page header of the Maths Repository's Word planners and the Quadrant Check's Word sheets. Daily Review slides stay as they are.

Colours

Your own colours: the main colour needs to be dark enough for white writing.
VLP Maths Tools Accent

Logo

No logo

PNG, JPG or SVG. It shows at the top left, beside the tool's name.

It shows beside the logo at the top of the tools, and in the page header of the Maths Repository's Word planners and the Quadrant Check's Word sheets.

Share it with your staff

Save a copy for your school downloads a copy of this file with your school name, colours, logo, format and data settings built in. Share that copy with your teachers, and it opens with them on every computer.

FormatBlocked

How your school sets out maths across the week. It changes the year overview in all three tabs.

Your blocked and 3 + 2 year overviews are kept separately, so switching back and forth loses nothing.

DataOff

Where the traffic lights on Maths Repository lessons come from. Choose one.

Switching keeps both sets of results: PAT uploads and marked checks stay in this browser and come back if you switch again.

SharePoint folderSave files straight into your school's SharePoint

Connect the Teaching and Learning folder that OneDrive syncs from your school's SharePoint site. The planners, lesson slides, Daily Review slides and Quadrant Checks you make are then saved into the folder of the sequence they belong to, so next year they are in the same place.

Lesson slides

The VLP lesson slides come in a separate file for each level. Add the levels you teach once, and the Maths Repository's Also download the lesson slides works for them on this computer.

Paste the link to the folder on your school drive (SharePoint, OneDrive, Google Drive or Teams). When a level's slides aren't added yet, the Maths Repository shows Open our school's slides folder with this link. Save a copy for your school (under Branding) builds it in for every teacher. A drive letter or network path (such as S:\Maths) is shown with a Copy button instead, because a browser can't open those from a link.

Levels on this computer

Choose one or more, for example VLP Maths Slides - Level 1.zip

From your school folder

Put the slides files in Teaching and Learning › Whole School › Tools › Lesson slides, once for the whole school. Every teacher who connects the Teaching and Learning folder (Settings › SharePoint folder) then gets them, read from the folder, with nothing to add on each computer.

Or use a slides folder (Chrome and Edge)

Point the tool at the folder where your school keeps the slides files, such as the shared drive. Every level in it is added, and new or updated levels in the folder are picked up. Your browser may ask now and then to allow access.

Keyboard shortcuts

  • 1 2 3 Maths Repository, Quadrant Check, Daily Review
  • Ctrl + Z Undo the last change to the year overview
  • Ctrl + P Print this tab (buttons and panels are left off)
  • S Save results, while marking a Quadrant Check
  • ? This list

Shortcuts don't apply while you're typing in a box.

What's new · you have Version 19, 12 November 2026

Version 20.0 · 24 November 2026

  • 20.1: connecting the Teaching and Learning folder always says what happened, including when the computer's browser settings don't let websites open folders.
  • The tools are on the web. Open them from one web address; a new version reaches everyone the next time they open it (a strip offers to reload if they have them open).
  • Your school's folder holds the VLP content. Connect the Teaching and Learning folder once: the tools read the VLP lessons, questions and programs (VLP Maths data - Primary.zip), the lesson slides and the retrieval slides from Whole School › VLP Resources, and save into each year level's folder as before.
  • No SharePoint folder, or using an iPad, Safari or Firefox? Choose the files instead, kept in that browser.
  • Moving from the HTML file: in it choose Back up, then bring the back-up in here, once.

Version 19.8 · 24 November 2026

  • Multi-age classes. A composite class can have 2 to 4 levels (click a level again to take it out). Its year overview has a row for each level in every term.
  • Program: the Department's mixed-age program (Levels 1 and 2, 3 and 4, 5 and 6), or Our own overview, which starts from each level's own program or blank. Build it by dragging sequences between weeks and terms, onto the shelf and back.
  • Combine units: click one sequence from each level, tick the lessons the class will be taught (all are ticked to start, with All and None for each sequence), and choose its weeks (4 lessons a week to start). The lessons are taught lowest level first. Click a combined unit to change its lessons or split it back into sequences. Sequences in its weeks move to free weeks, or to the shelf, and the overview says where.
  • The chosen lessons carry through: Plan these lessons ticks them in the Repository's planner in teaching order, and the Quadrant Check and Daily Review use only those lessons.
  • Daily Review for a composite class: one list for the whole class. One memory booster (the levels take turns), then four unit slots, each with one count. A combined unit counts once. Interleave stays in the options; backfill and the classroom compass are under More options.
  • The relief teacher pack is gone.

Version 19.7 · 19 November 2026

  • Repository: find lessons by content description code. Type a code such as VC2M3N04 (or part of one, such as N04) in the unit filter to see every unit with lessons that address it. The matching lessons are highlighted and tagged with the code, and each unit shows how many of its lessons match.

Version 19.6 · 19 November 2026

  • Year overview: sequence order check. When a sequence is moved earlier than a sequence it builds on at the same level, or that sequence is left out of the year, it's flagged: Out of order when several lessons rely on it, Check when only one or two do. Click a flag to see which lessons teach it and which use it, the shared content description, the Numeracy progression steps (each linked to the Australian Curriculum site), and the earlier-year sequences it rests on. Swap the two back, put a left-out sequence back in the year, or keep your order.

Version 19.5 · 19 November 2026

  • Repository: complete a unit plan. Tick Also complete a unit plan under Build to get a Word unit plan for each unit in the planner, in the VCAA teaching and learning unit template: the unit's content descriptions and achievement standards, the continuum of learning (the level before and after), the assessment, and a row for every lesson with its learning intention, success criteria, lesson elements, Enable and Extend, Inclusion and resources, set out by week. Cohort considerations, essential questions, moderation and the reflection are left for your team to complete. Choose 3, 4 or 5 lessons per week.
  • Repository: the planner starts at the lessons. The first page (overview, curriculum list and vocabulary) has been removed, so the Word document starts with the lessons.

Version 19.4 · 17 November 2026

  • Daily Review: Write my own. In + Add a slide, Write my own makes a review slide from the VLP templates (Classroom compass, Choice check, Think tank, Maths memory boosters) with the materials from the Retrieval Resources decks. The clock, ten frame, place value chart and part-part-whole model can be changed on the slide, and there are changeable tools for Levels 5 and 6 (number line, fraction bars, double number line, factor tree, function machine, table of values, Cartesian plane, angle, polygon, shapes with dimensions, prisms, column graph, dot plot, spinner, two dice grid). Add an answer slide if you want one.
  • Your school's slides are in Our slides at the top of + Add a slide, with an orange Our school tag. They go into a day only when a teacher adds them. With the school folder connected they are saved in the sequence's Daily Review › Our slides folder, so the whole team sees them.

Version 19.3 · 17 November 2026

  • Saving to the school folder: when a sequence's folder and file names make the path too long for Windows, the tool saves with a shorter name and says so, instead of saying the folder isn't on the computer.
  • The save box has a Close (×) and a Cancel button.
  • The planner's Not Covered by the VLPs box only appears when a unit in the planner has a supplementary lesson for that content.

Version 19.2 · 17 November 2026

  • Units you create yourself now only show in the tool for their level: a Level 3 unit made in the Primary tool no longer appears in the Secondary tool (and the other way round).
  • Lesson slides from your school folder. Put the VLP Maths Slides files in Teaching and Learning › Whole School › Tools › Lesson slides, once for the school. Every teacher who connects the Teaching and Learning folder (Settings › SharePoint folder) gets the slides for Also download the lesson slides, with nothing to add on each computer. They're read from the folder, so a file updated there is used straight away.
  • Adding a slides file in Settings › Lesson slides still works, for Edge or a computer without the folder.

Version 19 · 12 November 2026

  • 3 + 2: change how long a sequence runs. Drag a sequence's right edge to give it more or fewer weeks, as in the blocked overview (or press Shift and an arrow key). Its panel shows the weeks its lessons need, with a button to go back to them.
  • Any composite class. For two levels with no Department mixed-age program (for example Levels 4 and 5, or Foundation and Level 1), choose Our own composite program: a blank year overview with both levels' sequences on the shelf, to drag into the weeks you'll teach them. It works in the blocked and 3 + 2 overviews and in all three tabs. In the Daily Review and Quadrant Check, Each level's own program is still there.

Version 18.1 · 11 November 2026

  • Open the tools from your school's Teaching and Learning Hub (Google). When your school's hub has the tools, VLP tools › Open the VLP Maths Tools opens them in the browser with nothing to download or install, and files save straight into the hub's Drive folders, by sequence.

Version 18 · 10 November 2026

  • Save straight into your school's SharePoint. In Settings › SharePoint folder, connect the Teaching and Learning folder that OneDrive syncs from your school's site (Edge or Chrome). Files then go into the folder of the sequence they belong to: Year › Mathematics › S02 Multiplicative thinking › Lessons (planners and lesson slides), › Daily Review and › Assessment (Quadrant Check sheets and results).
  • A Daily Review or Quadrant Check goes to the sequence your year overview has for that week, or to Review and consolidation in a week with no new sequence. You see where before it saves, and can pick another year level or folder (handy for composite classes), or download it instead.
  • Folders are by sequence, not week, because the week a sequence is taught changes from year to year. The VLP Number Fact Fluency tool saves into the same folder, under Number fact fluency.

Version 17.1 · 9 November 2026

  • Clicking a sequence in the year overview now opens it in the unit list, with its lessons ready to tick. The lesson panel under the overview has gone. On the shelf, Enter adds a sequence to the year.

Version 17 · 5 November 2026

  • Choose adjustments beside the Inclusion boxes (Some students, Specific students) in Edit lesson and + Add your own lesson: tick reasonable adjustments from a list grouped by area (from the Department's guidance for students with disability), search it, or add your own. Your own adjustments are kept for next time.
  • Ticked adjustments go into the box, and from there into the Word planner's Inclusion row. Anything you type in the box is kept.
  • Save a copy for your school carries the adjustments you added, as Our school's adjustments for every teacher.

Version 16 · 5 November 2026

  • Create your own unit in the Maths Repository, for content the VLP doesn’t cover or to mix lessons from different sequences and levels. Use + Create your own unit on the shelf under the year overview or at the end of the unit list.
  • Give it a title, level and strand, then start empty, build it from VLP lessons (search every level and tick the lessons to copy) or plan it by hand. You can add check questions too.
  • Your unit is orange. It starts on the shelf in all three tabs; drag it into the year like any sequence. It takes 3 lessons a week for Number and Algebra and 2 a week for the other strands.
  • Its lessons have the usual Edit button. Copied lessons keep a link to the VLP lesson they came from, bring their VLP lesson slides and Daily Review slides, and bring the VLP summative questions on them to the Quadrant Check, with your check questions.
  • Edit unit changes its details and the order of its lessons; + Add a lesson adds more. Save my lessons and edits to a file, Our changes (Word) and Save a copy for your school all carry your units.

Version 15.3 · 5 November 2026

  • Daily Review: Interleave starts off, so each unit's slides sit together and are easy to check. Turn it on in the left-hand menu to mix the units; the tool remembers your choice.

Version 15.2 · 4 November 2026

  • Slides files for Foundation to Level 4 (Primary) Levels 7, 9 and 10 (Secondary, with the 10A units in Level 10; Level 7 in Primary too).
  • Lesson slides saved from Google Slides now download correctly.

Version 15.1 · 3 November 2026

  • Every option is shown again as standard, including the Daily Review's slots on the left (the units the slides come from, and how many slides from each), backfill, reteach lessons and units from other levels. Curriculum leaders can still hide options for staff in Settings › Branding (What your staff see).

Version 15 · 1 November 2026

  • Simpler to use: options can be tucked away until you click More options (top of the page). Curriculum leaders choose what staff see in Settings › Branding (What your staff see), and Save a copy for your school builds it in.
  • Three colours: VLP lessons are plain, lessons the tool adds (reteach, supplementary, another level) are blue, and your school's (edited, teacher created, planned by hand) are orange. A key sits under the units.
  • Back up (top of the page): one file with everything you've done in this browser, and Restore to put it back on any computer. A dot shows when there's work not backed up yet.
  • + Add your own lesson asks how to start: write it in full, copy a VLP lesson, or plan it by hand (an empty column in the planner, which replaces + Add a blank lesson).
  • Download remembers your choices (A3 or A4, slides, summative map), shown on one line with Change.
  • In a school copy, Settings shows teachers what they need; what the school set is listed, with Show all settings.
  • Drop a slides file anywhere on the page to add it.
  • Each tab's description is one line, with ? for more. A short welcome greets you the first time.
Earlier versions

Version 14 · 29 October 2026

  • Slides for teacher created lessons: Also download the lesson slides now makes slides from what you wrote (warm up, modelled example with your key diagram, your turn, check for understanding, independent practice and exit ticket), on the VLP slides’ own layouts, with a small orange Teacher created label.
  • Your own questions for an edited lesson: the edit form can add a Quadrant Check question and a Daily Review question, as well as the VLP’s, marked Your question. As for teacher created lessons, the tool won’t accept a question that repeats one from the lesson.
  • Our changes (Word) (above the units): one A4 document of every edited and teacher created lesson, with the VLP’s wording beside yours and an Approved box for each, for a PLC or curriculum leader to review before building edits into the school copy.

Version 13 · 29 October 2026

  • Edit any lesson in the Maths Repository: every lesson has an Edit button. It opens the same form as Add your own lesson, filled in with the lesson, so you can change its wording, steps, questions, success criteria, vocabulary or key diagram (add, change or remove the picture). Each changed row shows the VLP’s wording, so you can put it back.
  • An edited lesson’s button turns purple and reads Edited. In the Word planner the lesson has your wording, with a purple border round its number and title.
  • Save my lessons and edits to a file shares your edits with your team, and Save a copy for your school (Settings › Branding) builds them in for every teacher. The Quadrant Check, Daily Review and lesson slides keep the VLP’s own questions and slides.

Version 12 · 28 October 2026

  • The lesson slides are now a separate file for each level (for example VLP Maths Slides - Level 8.zip), so this file is much smaller and opens faster. The first time you tick Also download the lesson slides for a level, choose that level's slides file. It's kept on this computer, so you're only asked once.
  • Settings › Lesson slides: the levels on this computer, add or remove slides files, or (in Chrome and Edge) use your school's slides folder. Schools can add a link to where they keep the slides files, and Save a copy for your school builds it in.
  • Slides files so far: Foundation, Level 1, Level 2, Level 3, Level 4, Level 5, Level 6, Level 7.

Version 11 · 27 October 2026

  • Also download the lesson slides (Maths Repository, under the planner's download options): one PowerPoint with the VLP slides for the lessons you've ticked, in the planner's order, even when they come from different sequences. Every slide is copied unchanged from the VLP lesson PowerPoints, with a title slide before each lesson.

Version 10 · 24 October 2026

  • Add your own lesson to any VLP sequence (Maths Repository › open a sequence › + Add your own lesson). It sits in the sequence in orange under a Teacher created banner, with the same rows as the VLP lessons, and goes into the Word planner. Start from a blank form or copy a VLP lesson's rows.
  • It can give the Quadrant Check a check question and the Daily Review a review slide (after it has been taught). You write both questions: the tool won't accept one that repeats a question from the lesson.
  • Your lessons are kept in this browser. Save my lessons to a file (above the units) keeps a copy and shares them with your team.

Version 9 · 23 October 2026

  • One class and week bar under the heading in every tab: the class level, Composite, the week and This week, in the same place and style.
  • Quadrant Check › Mark the sheet has three views: Mark a check, Class progress (every lesson checked this term, last term or this year, with its result in each check and the trend, who keeps appearing in Tier 2, and how red lessons did when rechecked) and Student history (each student across class-grid checks). Both download as Excel.
  • Recheck after reteach: Make the sheet offers the red questions from the class's last check, to put back on this sheet.
  • Print a blank class grid to tick by hand while marking (Mark the sheet › Class grid).
  • Relief teacher pack: each day now also has that day's lesson summary from the Maths Repository.
  • Search every level in the Maths Repository: type a lesson or sequence name to find it at any level.
  • Keyboard shortcuts (press ?): 1, 2, 3 switch tabs; S saves marks; Ctrl+P prints the tab you're on, without the buttons.

Version 8 · 23 October 2026

  • Quadrant Check: Make the sheet | Mark the sheet. Two steps at the top of the tab. Mark the sheet opens the marking straight away, with the steps to follow (and a Word copy of them to download), the class and week being marked, and Marked before chips to reopen an earlier check. The bar with Save results stays at the bottom of the window and says when results aren't saved.
  • Marks are never lost by mistake. Marks not yet saved are kept until you close the browser, even if you change the week, the class or the tab; you're reminded to save them.
  • Hide overview in every tab: the year overview folds away to its title and stays folded until you show it again.
  • One look for all three tabs: the Maths Repository now has the same heading and page width as the other two, so its 3 + 2 year overview fits its box.

Version 7 · 21 October 2026

  • Data: Quadrant Check. In Settings › Data, choose where the Maths Repository's traffic lights come from: PAT Maths or Quadrant Check.
  • Mark this check (Quadrant Check tab, under the sheet): enter the results by quick tally (how many got each question right) or class grid (✓, ½, ✗ or absent for each student). It suggests next steps for each quadrant and, with the class grid, a possible Tier 2 group.
  • In the Maths Repository, each lesson a question came from gets a light (green 80% or more, amber 50–79%, red under 50%) from the latest check that included it, with its earlier results. The panel lists the checks marked and suggests what to do next. Suggestions only: nothing changes until you choose to.
  • Add to review on a Quadrant Check suggestion (2 weeks ago, 4 weeks ago, A year ago) adds 2 slides a day from that sequence to the class's Daily Review, for two weeks (four for A year ago). Those slides are tagged From Quadrant Check; change or remove them under Backfill in the Daily Review.
  • Download as Excel: one check (in the Quadrant Check tab) or every marked check (in the Maths Repository), with each student's marks for class-grid checks.

Version 6 · 21 October 2026

  • Settings (top of the page) replaces the Year overview and Branding buttons. It has four sections: Year overview, Branding, Format and Data.
  • Format: 3 + 2. Each week, 3 Number and algebra lessons and 2 Measurement, space, statistics and probability lessons. The year overview in every tab has two rows a term, so two sequences run side by side. Click a sequence to split it into parts (as many as you like) and drag each part to where you'll teach it. The Repository orders lessons 3 + 2 and marks each week; the Daily Review reviews both current sequences; the Quadrant Check checks both rows in every quadrant. Blocked keeps the Department's program, and switching back loses nothing.
  • Data: PAT Maths. Upload your class's PAT Maths results in the Maths Repository and each lesson gets a traffic light. The panel shows the date the class sat each test (enter it if the file doesn't say) and recommends the year-level test over the adaptive test.
  • Save a copy for your school (under Branding) now carries the format and data settings too.

Opening…

    Setting this up for your school?

    In Settings, add your school's name, logo and colours, choose Blocked or 3 + 2, and choose where class results come from (PAT Maths or Quadrant Check). Then Save a copy for your school and share that copy with staff: it opens set up the same way for everyone.
